transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because... well, I just can't shake this thought I keep having. I've been an electrician for years, and if all that experience couldn't keep my own brother safe, then... I don't know. I just feel like I'm a danger to anybody who works with me, or even anyone who lives under my roof.
Would you say that this thought about being a danger to others is something that pops into your head against your will?

Yes, but it's more than just a thought popping up. It's... it's like I'm actually there again. I'll be in the middle of wiring a panel at work, or... or I'll just be at home and hear my nephew shut the garage door, and suddenly I'm right back there. I can smell the smoke, I can see my brother... it's like the whole job site just drops out from under me and I'm reliving it. It just takes over.
Have you been avoiding certain places, activities, or situations because of these memories or thoughts?

Yeah. I mean... I don't even go in my own garage anymore unless I absolutely have to. I just stay out of there. I also quit helping with the electrical stuff at my church. And if people bring up... you know, if they start talking about car projects, or the fire, I shut them down fast. I just can't be around any of it.
Do you experience any physical symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or trembling when these memories take over?

No, I don't think so. I mean, my heart might beat a little faster when I get startled, but I haven't really noticed any sweating or shaking or anything like that when the memories happen. It's mostly just the feeling of being right back there.
Do you feel guilty about what happened to your brother?

Yeah. I mean... yeah, definitely. There's just this heavy mix of guilt and anger sitting in my chest all day long. It's... it's especially bad when I look at my nephew. I just think about how he lost his dad and got stuck with me instead. It's hard to shake that feeling.
How long have you been experiencing these memories and feelings of guilt?
It's been about four months now. Basically ever since the garage fire happened and my nephew came to live with me. It's just been a constant thing since then.
Are there any specific people you've been avoiding since the fire happened?

Not really specific people, I guess. It's more about what they bring up. Like, I shut people down fast if they start talking about car projects or the fire. I just won't entertain it. I also quit helping out with the church electrical stuff, so I guess I've been avoiding the folks over there. And... honestly, I don't even go in my own garage anymore unless I absolutely have to.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy doing?

I don't think so... not really. I mean, besides the things I just mentioned, like the car projects and the church volunteering. I definitely don't have any desire to do those anymore. But other than that, I haven't really noticed. I just... I mostly just go to work and try to take care of my nephew. I don't really do much else these days.
Are there any activities that you used to find enjoyable or fulfilling before the fire, but now find you have little to no interest in?

I mean, I think that's pretty much what I just mentioned. It's really just the car projects and the volunteer work at the church. Other than that... no, not that I can think of. I just don't really have the drive for much else besides my job and making sure my nephew is taken care of right now.
Are there any other activities besides car projects and church volunteering that you've lost interest in since the fire happened?

No, like I said, there really isn't anything else. I didn't have a whole lot of hobbies to begin with. My life was pretty much just my job, the cars, helping at the church, and taking care of my nephew. So... no, nothing else comes to mind.
Have you noticed yourself pulling back from social interactions or relationships since the fire happened?

No, I haven't really noticed that. I mean, I still talk to the guys on the job site just fine. And I'm obviously around my nephew all the time. Like I said, I didn't have a massive group of friends to begin with, so... I don't feel like I'm avoiding anybody or pulling away from people. I'm just doing my usual routine of going to work and coming home.
Do you find yourself constantly on the lookout for potential dangers or threats, even when you're not working with electricity?

No, not really. I mean, obviously at work I have to be careful, you know, checking the lines and making sure everything's grounded. That's just the job. But outside of that... no, I don't think I'm constantly looking over my shoulder or anything. I just go about my day.
Do you often find yourself being easily startled by small things, like a loud noise?

No, I can't say that I do. I mean, working on a job site, you get used to a lot of sudden noise anyway... guys dropping tools, machinery starting up. So, no, a loud noise doesn't really jump me. I haven't noticed being easily startled or anything like that.
Do you have trouble falling or staying asleep at night?

Yeah, sleep is... it's pretty bad. Most nights I just lie there in the dark, listening. Like I'm waiting to hear that crackling sound again, or even just a car door shutting in the driveway. And when I finally do manage to drop off, I end up jolting awake, just completely soaked in sweat from dreaming about the garage. After that, I usually can't get back to sleep before I have to get up for work.
Do you feel like you're always on edge, even when there's no apparent reason to be?

No, not really. I mean... I don't feel tense all the time or anything like that. During the day, when I'm working or just running errands, I feel pretty normal. It's really just the nighttime that messes with me, like I was saying. But during the day? No, I wouldn't say I'm on edge.
Do you find yourself always being very aware of your surroundings, even when there's no need to be?

No, not really. I mean, I pay attention to what I'm doing at work, obviously, since I'm dealing with electrical panels and all that. But outside of that... no, I'm not constantly scanning the room or looking over my shoulder. When I'm out running errands or whatever, I just mind my own business. I don't feel like I'm overly focused on everything going on around me.
Do you ever have moments where you feel like you're reliving the garage fire, but without being triggered by something specific like a smell or a sound?

Yeah, actually. Sometimes it's exactly like that, just out of nowhere. I'll be... I'll be in the middle of wiring a panel at work, completely focused on what I'm doing, and suddenly it's like the whole job site just drops out from under me. I'm right back there, smelling the smoke and seeing my brother. 

But sometimes it is a sound that does it, too. Like if I hear my nephew shut the garage door... it just hits me all at once and I'm right back in it.
Have you noticed a decrease in interest in activities you used to enjoy since the fire happened, beyond just the car projects and church volunteering?

No, I haven't really noticed anything else. The car projects and the church volunteering were pretty much my main hobbies outside of work anyway. I mean, I still watch sports on TV and do stuff around the house like I normally would. So... no, beyond those two things you mentioned, I wouldn't say I've lost interest in anything else.
